title: Google DeepMind, Google Cloud to allow European researchers access to frontier models
source_used: Reuters wire, text read in Central Oregon Daily's copy; same facts in Channel NewsAsia as relayed by UA.NEWS
key_facts: Brussels, 14 Oct 2026 (Reuters): Google DeepMind and Alphabet's cloud service Google Cloud will give up to 200 European scientific researchers direct access to their frontier models.
The access comes with $3 million in compute credits, the companies said on Wednesday.
Tools named: AlphaFold 3, WeatherNext, AlphaGenome, AlphaEvolve and AlphaEarth Foundations.
The companies said it will help researchers tackle complex challenges faster, from predicting extreme weather to mapping molecular structures.
The wire does not say how researchers will be chosen or how the credits are shared.
quote_evidence: Google DeepMind and Alphabet's cloud service Google Cloud will provide up to 200 European scientific researchers with direct access to their frontier models, together with $3 million in compute credits, the U.S. tech giant said on Wednesday.
The move will give researchers direct access to the companies' scientific tools including AlphaFold 3, WeatherNext, AlphaGenome, AlphaEvolve, and AlphaEarth Foundations.
why_it_matters_hint: European scientists get direct access to Google's most advanced science AI tools, but the scheme is capped at 200 researchers.
notes: Reuters site returned HTTP 401; text read in a carried copy of the Reuters wire. Company announcement reported by Reuters, with the same facts in Channel NewsAsia (via UA.NEWS).
